passages.title: Service flows of Dinsos P2PA Demak (Puskesos, SLRT, violence, disaster, disability, adoption and more), English translation of the office's public infographics
passages.text: 1. Puskesos complaint flow 1. A resident comes in or submits a complaint: needs, problems or complaints go to the Puskesos (village social welfare centre) manager in person, by phone or through complaint media. 2. Registration and verification: the officer records the resident's identity and does an initial check of the complaint. 3. Identifying the need: the officer identifies the type of need or problem, such as social aid, health, education, civil registration or other social services. 4. Referral or coordination: if needed, Puskesos coordinates with or refers the resident to the relevant government office, agency or institution. 5. Follow-up: the officer monitors and helps resolve the resident's problem. 6. Completion and records: the result is recorded in the Puskesos administration and the resident is told the outcome.

passages.text: 2. SLRT flow: certificate of registration in the DTKS / poverty database The Integrated Service and Referral System (SLRT) accepts requests in person, by phone, WhatsApp, email or the suggestion box. 1. The service user applies for a certificate of registration in DTKS (now DTSEN) or the poverty database. 2. Data recording and initial verification: the SLRT team records the applicant's data and checks the requirements. General requirements: copy of the ID card (KTP), copy of the family card (KK), the application form, and supporting documents if needed. 3. Coordination with the sub-coordinator, head of division or head of office and the team: administrative check and data check in the DTKS/DTSEN system, with a field visit if needed. 4. The analysis is written up from the data and checks; a follow-up plan form is made if needed. 5.

passages.text: 3. SLRT flow: PBI-Pemda / UHC health insurance recommendation 1. A resident applies for a PBI-Pemda / UHC (government-paid health insurance) recommendation through SLRT, in person, by letter, suggestion box, WhatsApp or email. 2. The SLRT team records the complaint or request in the system and the SLRT form. 3. The SLRT team reports the recap to the sub-coordinator, head of division and head of office. 4. Coordination and handling: administrative check and field visit if needed. 5. Eligibility analysis based on the checks and coordination with the parties involved. 6. A follow-up plan form for the PBI-Pemda / UHC recommendation is prepared. 7. The PBI-Pemda / UHC recommendation is issued and given to the applicant.

passages.text: 4. SLRT flow: BPJS employment insurance claims for vulnerable workers 1. Complaints, suggestions or input are submitted in writing through the suggestion box, SMS or email. 2. Suggestion box, SMS and email submissions are collected. 3. The team gathers the users' complaints. 4. The head of division instructs the team to carry out administrative and factual checks. 5. The recap is reported and coordinated with the manager. 6. The team records the complaints, suggestions and input. 7. The results of the checks are analysed. 8. The head of division and the team agree a follow-up plan (old-age savings, work accident and death benefits for vulnerable workers).

passages.text: 5. Handling violence against women and children 1. Report by the service user: in person, by letter, phone or complaint media. 2. First response in parallel: coordination and first support with the police women and children unit (Unit PPA Polres); counselling and first psychosocial support; a home visit if needed to assess the victim. 3. Medical examination (visum) at a health facility. 4. Problem analysis: needs and a handling plan. 5. Psychological support: further counselling and recovery support. 6. Legal aid: support through the legal process and access to related services. If the victim is in danger now, call 110 (police) or SAPA 129 (WhatsApp 08111-129-129).

passages.text: 6. Aid for victims of natural and social disasters 1. Start. 2. The request for aid is submitted to the Regent through Dinas Sosial P2PA; the request is received and processed. 3. Site visit to the disaster location. 4. Assessment of the site visit. 5. Identifying the recipients' needs and the type of aid. 6. Deciding the amount of aid for the victims. 7. Approving the amount; if not approved, it is discussed again. 8. Preparing the relief goods according to need. 9. Distributing the aid to the victims according to need. 10. Documenting the handover as evidence. 11. Recording the time, place, type and amount of aid distributed. 12. End.

passages.text: 7. Social rehabilitation service for people with disabilities 1. Complaint from or about a person with a disability: in person, by letter, phone or complaint media. 2. The officer receives the complaint: recording and initial verification. 3. The officer carries out an assessment of the person's needs and condition. Possible services: health (examination and medical referral), psychological (counselling), legal (legal aid and support), social (social support and empowerment), economic (training, access to work, economic aid). 4. Assessment result: discussion and a service plan; family reunification support where the family needs strengthening. 5. Referral to the relevant service or institution. 6. Completion: monitoring and follow-up.

passages.text: 8. Referring homeless people and beggars to a social rehabilitation centre 1. The officer receives homeless people, beggars or neglected people from the municipal police (Satpol PP), the police or other agencies. 2. The officer identifies and records them; the case is rejected or accepted. 3. The officer gives counselling. 4. The officer prepares an intervention plan. 5. The officer carries out the intervention (guidance). 6. The officer evaluates, closes and refers: back to the family or to a social rehabilitation centre (Balai Rehabsos). 7. The officer gives follow-up guidance through home visits.

passages.text: 9. Admission to the shelter (rumah singgah) 1. The officer receives a report from the public; rejected if the criteria are not met, accepted if they are. 2. The officer identifies and selects prospective beneficiaries. 3. The officer assesses the beneficiary (interview, observation and needs review). 4. The officer prepares an intervention plan. 5. The officer carries out the intervention (support, basic needs, mental and social strengthening). 6. The officer evaluates, closes and refers: back to the family (reunification) or to a social rehabilitation centre. 7. The officer gives follow-up guidance through home visits to make sure the service continues and the beneficiary recovers.

passages.text: 10. Recommendation on child marriage (early marriage) 1. The applicant requests a recommendation on an early (child) marriage and completes the requirements. 2. The administrative officer receives and checks the documents. 3. Coordination with the head of the child marriage prevention working group (POKJA KHPK). 4. A service officer (social worker or psychologist) provides service, assessment and support to the applicant. 5. Eligibility analysis: the assessment, social and psychological conditions and related aspects. 6. If found eligible, a recommendation letter is issued. 7. The letter is handed to the applicant for use according to the rules.

passages.text: 11. Child adoption 1. Prospective adoptive parents come to the social rehabilitation division and hand in the required documents. 2. The officer checks the documents; incomplete or ineligible files are returned with an explanation. 3. The officer makes a home visit for initial verification and assessment. 4. The officer prepares the adoption approval letter. 5. The officer makes a second verification home visit. 6. The officer issues the adoption recommendation letter.

passages.title: Sample complaint response standard for Dinsos P2PA Demak (written for this demo from PermenPANRB 5/2025)
passages.text: 1. Receiving complaints Complaints are accepted from every channel: in person (Puskesos, SLRT, the office), letter, phone, WhatsApp, email, suggestion box, social media, SP4N-LAPOR! and Embrace chat. Every complaint gets a ticket number and an acknowledgement. Filing a complaint is free. The complainant's personal data is kept confidential.

passages.title: Sample complaint response standard for Dinsos P2PA Demak (written for this demo from PermenPANRB 5/2025)
passages.text: 2. Emergencies Emergencies: violence happening now, a woman or child thrown out of their home, a family with no food today or nowhere to sleep tonight, victims of floods, tidal floods (rob) or fire who have not evacuated, people with mental illness who are chained (pasung) or neglected, and threats of suicide. Emergency complaints go straight to the duty supervisor and get a response within 2 hours at most. For violence against women and children, the UPTD PPA officer coordinates with the police women and children unit and points to SAPA 129. Late social aid alone is not an emergency.

passages.title: Sample complaint response standard for Dinsos P2PA Demak (written for this demo from PermenPANRB 5/2025)
passages.text: 3. Follow-up deadlines Following PermenPANRB 5/2025 Article 21: 5 working days for information requests and normative complaints; 14 working days for complaints that need no field inspection; 60 working days for complaints that need oversight and a field inspection. If the complainant's data is incomplete, the officer asks for it; complaints not completed within 10 working days are archived.

passages.title: Sample complaint response standard for Dinsos P2PA Demak (written for this demo from PermenPANRB 5/2025)
passages.text: 4. Social aid not received (PKH, BPNT/Sembako, BLT) The Social Protection and Security officer checks within 3 working days: the recipient's status in DTSEN, the payment status for the current round, and the status of the KKS card or bank account. If several residents of one village report the same problem, the officer checks the whole payment round and coordinates with the PKH companion and the e-warong shop.

passages.title: Sample complaint response standard for Dinsos P2PA Demak (written for this demo from PermenPANRB 5/2025)
passages.text: 5. Illegal levies and distribution fraud Aid recipients never have to pay anything. Reports of illegal levies by e-warong agents, group leaders or village officials are recorded without revealing the reporter's identity, checked by the distribution oversight team, and passed to the Inspectorate or law enforcement if proven.

passages.text: 6. DTSEN data and certificates Registration, status checks and data corrections in DTSEN (formerly DTKS) are handled by SLRT or Puskesos; bring your ID card (KTP) and family card (KK). Wrong data, such as a family member who has died, is corrected through the village office. See the SLRT flow.

Melakukan peninjauan di lokasi terjadinya bencana. 4. Mengkaji hasil peninjauan di lokasi bencana. 5. Mengidentifikasi kebutuhan penerima bantuan dan jenis bantuan yang akan diberikan. 6. Mencatat waktu penyaluran, lokasi penyaluran, jenis barang bantuan, jumlah, dan lain-lain. 12. Selesai.

Petugas menerima aduan: pencatatan dan verifikasi awal. 3. Petugas melakukan asesmen: identifikasi kebutuhan dan kondisi penyandang disabilitas. Layanan yang dapat diberikan: layanan kesehatan (pemeriksaan dan rujukan medis), layanan psikologis (konseling), layanan hukum (bantuan dan pendampingan hukum), layanan sosial (pendampingan dan pemberdayaan), layanan ekonomi (pelatihan, akses usaha, bantuan ekonomi). 4. Hasil asesmen: pembahasan dan penetapan rencana layanan; layanan reunifikasi keluarga bagi yang memerlukan penguatan fungsi keluarga. 5. Layanan rujukan sesuai kebutuhan ke layanan atau lembaga terkait. 6. Selesai: pemantauan dan tindak lanjut.

Petugas menerima tuna sosial (gelandangan, pengemis, orang terlantar) dari Satpol PP, Kepolisian, atau instansi terkait. 2. Petugas melakukan identifikasi dan seleksi calon Penerima Manfaat. 3. Petugas melaksanakan asesmen ke Penerima Manfaat (wawancara, observasi, dan kajian kebutuhan). 4.
